01 · EDA: estimating the visibility of social media posts¶

Question: can we estimate how many people saw a post better than Brand24's rule reach ≈ constant × followers, and how sure can we be?

Step Question
1 What data do we have, and where does it come from?
2 Where do we know the true visibility?
3 What do reach values look like? Any outliers?
4 How does Brand24's constant behave?
5 What is related to reach?
6 Could a better estimator work?
7 Takeaways

1 · The data¶

Source: reach_samples_students.csv, a sample of brand mentions collected by Brand24 (raw file, read-only). One row = one mention of a brand on one platform.

Role Columns Used for
Target b24_estimated_reach what Brand24 reports today
Ground truth view_count real visibility (only some platforms)
Predictors author_followers, likes, comments, shares inputs of an estimator
Context platform, brand, language, country, sentiment, created_at splits, bias checks
Not used author_name, author_url, url personal data (GDPR), never shown 
12,500 mentions · 348 brands · 2025-01 → 2026-10
platform tiktok youtube twitter facebook instagram
mentions 2500 2500 2500 2500 2500 
From April 2026 on: 66% of mentions · English: 85%

Takeaway: missing values depend on the platform, not on chance. Facebook and Instagram have no views; Instagram rarely has followers. Most mentions are recent and in English, so the sample is not uniform in time or language.

2 · Where do we know the true visibility?¶

views known % reach = views %
platform
tiktok 100.00 100.00
youtube 99.00 100.00
twitter 75.00 2.00
facebook 0.00 NaN
instagram 0.00 NaN

Takeaway: on TikTok and YouTube all points sit on the diagonal: reach is the view count, so this is our ground truth. On Twitter, views exist for most posts but reach is a separate estimate. Facebook and Instagram have no views, so estimates there cannot be checked directly.

3 · Reach values and outliers¶

median mean / median zeros % top 1% posts hold % of reach
platform
tiktok 723.00 40.30 0.40 61.60
youtube 397.00 60.70 1.50 71.90
twitter 141.00 16.10 11.20 42.40
facebook 2,200.00 9.10 8.90 42.50
instagram 20.00 138.30 43.40 80.30

Takeaway: very skewed. A few viral posts hold a large part of all reach (up to 80% for the top 1% on Instagram). We work on the log scale with medians. Outliers are kept: on TikTok/YouTube they are real viral posts. Instagram has many zeros.

4 · How does Brand24's constant behave?¶

If reach = constant × followers, then reach / followers should be one number per platform.

twitter: most common ratios → {0.1: 968, 0.09: 246, 0.08: 56, 0.07: 47, 0.05: 42}
facebook: most common ratios → {0.04: 377, 0.1: 325, 0.06: 304, 0.02: 176, 0.05: 173}

Takeaway: on Twitter the ratio has a sharp peak at one value. On Facebook it takes several values and drops for bigger accounts. So the "constant" is a platform-specific, step-wise rule. This rule is the baseline to beat.

5 · What is related to reach?¶

Takeaway: each platform has a different driver (Facebook reach follows followers, Instagram reach follows likes). One global multiplier is unlikely to fit all. Blank cells = no data or no variation. Correlation, not causation.

6 · Could a better estimator work?¶

Where real views exist, we predict views out of sample (5-fold CV, log10 scale) and compare: (a) followers × constant · (b) followers only · (c) followers + likes + comments + shares.

platform tiktok youtube twitter
model
(a) followers × constant 0.93 0.83 0.78
(b) followers 0.61 0.78 0.59
(c) + engagement 0.28 0.57 0.48

Takeaway: adding engagement clearly lowers the error on all three platforms; the points move closer to the diagonal. Preliminary: no tuning, no grouping by brand, and it says nothing yet about Facebook/Instagram.

7 · Takeaways¶

What we learned

  • 12,500 mentions, 2,500 per platform; missing data depends on the platform.
  • Ground truth (views) exists only on TikTok and YouTube (partly Twitter).
  • Reach is extremely skewed, so we use the log scale, medians and quantiles.
  • Brand24's "constant" is a step-wise, per-platform rule, which gives a clear baseline.
  • Engagement adds information beyond followers where we can test it.

What we will use: target view_count / reach (log10) · inputs: followers, likes, comments, shares, platform · baseline: Brand24's rule.

Main limits: no ground truth on Facebook/Instagram · reach there may just repeat Brand24's own formula · sample is uneven in time.

Next: grouped CV by brand + prediction intervals · measure the error of Brand24's rule on Twitter · M1 card.
